attributes.name: authorized file UUID
attributes.knownFrom: File > Manage > Security > Advanced Settings > File Access > the file list (FileMaker identifies an authorised file by its file UUID, which no dialog shows). SaXML location not yet located: the FileAccessCatalog writes no UUID for the paired file, and fm’s uuid is not the Authorization element’s own UUID either - ids 3 and 4, the inbound/outbound pair created together for TestFile_dev, both read 0A60AFFF-C849-4680-A7D8-6CD2FCDA30E8 while their UUID elements are 6020A44F… and 21681789…. That value is also Ooe.fmp12’s own root UUID, which is not fm echoing the local file: a copied file keeps its identity, and Ooe-patched.fmp12 carries the same UUID. The rest of the export corroborates the reading - A049B832-732C-4386-937B-4B904D211067, shared by ids 5 and 6, is BrojDva.fmp12’s root UUID, and F1D61AC2-B2C3-4B99-AD24-B983FF539B1C (id 7) is sandbox.fmp12’s. So the key is the paired file’s identity, one value per file, which corrects docs/saxml-inventory.md line 396 ("fm exposes no per-object UUID outside graphNote and authorization"). Under-evidenced: fmai’s probe sets bit 19 when it writes false (32 -> 524320) and sets bits 19 AND 10 when it writes true (32 -> 525344), so bit 19 records only that the option was touched and bit 10 carries the value. Ooe cannot separate them — Concealed Edit Box object 133 carries both bits — so this row keeps the bit-19 mapping and the bit-10 half sits in the undecoded-bits row

attributes.name: show navigation dots
attributes.knownFrom: SaXML LayoutCatalog SlideControl/Options bit 0; Inspector > Position > Slide Control > Show navigation dots. Bit set means OFF. fmai agrees: its probe wrote showNavigationDots=false and recorded setMeansTrue=true, i.e. the bit is SET after writing false (0 -> 1), so a set bit means the option is off. The evidence confirms it: Ooe’s slide control writes SlideControl/Options="0" and fm reports showNavigationDots true

attributes.name: enable swipe gestures
attributes.knownFrom: SaXML LayoutCatalog SlideControl/Options bit 1; Inspector > Position > Slide Control > Enable swipe gestures. Bit set means OFF. fmai agrees: its probe wrote enableSwipeGestures=false and recorded setMeansTrue=true, i.e. the bit is SET after writing false (0 -> 2), so a set bit means the option is off. The evidence confirms it: the word is 0 and fm reports enableSwipeGestures true

attributes.name: built-in privilege set
attributes.knownFrom: SaXML PrivilegeSetsCatalog access@default; File > Manage > Security > Advanced Settings > Privilege Sets > Edit Privilege Set; the flag is written on exactly the three privilege sets FileMaker creates with every file ([Full Access] 1, [Data Entry Only] 2, [Read-Only Access] 3) and on none of Ooe’s four custom sets (4, 5, 6, 7), which is exactly the split fm reports as builtIn. FileMaker refuses to save an edit to a built-in set, which is the same fact. The probe is a custom set, so the attribute itself is absent there while fm reports builtIn false. Verified read-only on 2026-09-14 against the same file with one extra batch of describe ops covering every account, privilege set, extended privilege and authorization in Ooe, run with the same flags the check uses.

attributes.name: bit 0x80 of the options word (With dialog: Off)
attributes.knownFrom: SaXML ScriptCatalog StepsForScripts Script/ObjectList/Step[@id=42] Options bit 0x80; Script Workspace > the Page Setup step’s options; fm carries this option in NO key of its own — only the raw word. FileMaker prints: clear → With dialog: On, set → With dialog: Off. attributes.name: tokenised field and custom-function references of a formula
attributes.knownFrom: fm `references` — the tokens the formula refers to, one object per reference, emitted only when the op is sent `references: true` and only on the valid branch. New in fm 0.8.0-beta.0 (29827611); 0.7.0 named no token of the formula it had just parsed. PARTIAL against the SaXML chunk list this row is drawn from: fm reports FieldReference as {kind:"field", name, occurrence, id} — so the occurrence rides along with the field rather than being its own token — and CustomFunctionRef as {kind:"customFunction", name, id}. It reports NO token for a variable, a built-in function, a plug-in function or a script. Probed live on 2026-09-20: `Contacts::Name & $local & $$GLOBAL` returns the Name field alone; `GFN ( Contacts::Name )` returns the custom function and the field; `Length ( Contacts::Name )` returns the field only; `BE_Version` returns []. The plug-in half is tracked as its own gap on `plugin-call-sites`

attributes.name: tokenised variable references of a formula
attributes.knownFrom: NOT REPORTED. fm 0.8.0-beta.0's `references` tokenises a formula's fields and its custom-function calls and nothing else: probed live on 2026-09-20, `Contacts::Name & $local & $$GLOBAL` returns the Name field alone, naming neither variable. So FileMaker's own VariableReference chunk has no counterpart here, and "which formulas read this $$ global" is answerable only by scanning calculation text. Keyed on the element field rather than on `references` itself so that the row CLOSES the day fm emits a variable token, rather than having to be noticed by a human first. The `variable` spelling is inferred from the two kinds fm does emit (`field`, `customFunction`); if fm chooses another word the row stays open, which understates coverage rather than overstating it

attributes.name: what the formula was validated as (fm only)

attributes.name: evaluation context resolved (fm only)

attributes.name: plug-in function call site in a formula
attributes.knownFrom: SaXML DDR_INFO writes a FunctionRef chunk for a call to a plug-in function. STILL A GAP in fm 0.8.0-beta.0 (29827611), and now for a sharper reason than before: this build loads the installed plug-ins (its stderr names BaseElements.fmplugin among four) and so parses `BE_Version` as a VALID formula, where 0.7.0 called it invalid with `table_missing` for an unresolvable reference. But asked with `references: true` — the key 0.8.0 added for exactly this question — the same probe returns `references: []`. fm therefore knows enough about the call to accept it and still will not say the call site is there, so a formula's plug-in call sites cannot be recovered from fm.

attributes.name: formula is valid (fm only)

New in fm 0.7.0 (29823677), and the key to branch on: the line reports status "ok" whenever the QUESTION could be answered, so an invalid formula is `"status":"ok"` with `"valid":false`. attributes.name: validation error (fm only)
attributes.knownFrom: fm `error` — why the formula is invalid, as {code, engineCode, message, errorBegin, errorEnd}; errorBegin/errorEnd bracket the offending characters. New in fm 0.7.0 (29823677), which reported code "table_missing", engine code 106, over characters 0–10 ("BE_Version"). NOT EXERCISED since fm 0.8.0-beta.0 (29827611): the probe formula now validates, and fm's help for validate:calculation states that the invalid branch is what carries these keys — "emitted only when `valid` is false, so the key means something when it appears". Absence here is a fact about the probe, not about fm.
